newsitem.title: USA: Solv-ex cuts staff at portions of plant.
newsitem.headline: Solv-ex cuts staff at portions of plant.

text.p: Solv-Ex Corp said on Monday it laid off approximately 240 employees whose work on portions of an oil production plant is now complete or where the continuing work requires a diminished work force.
The reduction in the plant construction work force is in accordance with the company's plans for concentrating on first stage oil production, planned for the first quarter of 1997, the company said.
Approximately 240 employees remain at the plant, Solv-Ex said.
Solv-Ex said it plans to begin construction of a synthetic minerals processing plant, an expansion of the oil production facility and an aluminum plant, once oil production commences.
Company representatives were not immediately available for comment about whether the company is reporting a charge against earnings or any cost savings related to the job cuts.

Solv-Ex president Jack Butler said the company does not anticipate taking a charge in connection with the job cuts also the costs associated with the employees were considered part of the company's capital budget to build the facility.
The plant in Alberta, Canada is initially expected to produce 15,000 barrels of oil per day and the company is hoping to expand the facility, Butler said.

The company uses a unique process that separates oil from sand and clay, Butler said. The company's process does not create environmental problems associated with other forms of oil exploration, Butler said.
